answer: The door displays a QR code that rotates every thirty seconds, and the lantern of the design is that scanning it proves the attendee was at the door in that exact half-minute. The kernel of the scheme is that a screenshot of an old code is rejected, so the proof is fresh by construction. A Sybil cannot share a screenshot with a friend outside, because the garden of the rotation makes the code expire before it can be forwarded and used.
